title: Global vendor engine bridge crosses concurrent native run provider and billing identities

evidence.note: Independent 8c fixture reproduced both original run requests sent to tenant-B engine; ba91 still has same global closures. Native handoff restriction test at ba91 also fails after vendor run returns.

trigger_path: Concurrent startRun A/B replaces shared vendor prototype with B closure; A uses B provider/sink. Native handoff starts after VideoStudio restriction scope closes.

assertions.given: Concurrent native vendor requests, direct/routed transports, nested runs, custom structured options, absent/closed/tampered scope
assertions.expect: Each run keeps its own engine/provider/billing sink; no-scope, late and tampered dispatcher calls perform zero external submissions; all adapter options and source limits persist through native handoff.

fix_plan: Install only fixed vendor dispatchers, route through AsyncLocalStorage with active run engine and closed lifecycle. Native task wraps full runner, and marketing limits cover post-vendor handoff. Correct reasonStructured three-argument forwarding.
blast_radius: Native preproduction model calls and billing sink scopes; no vendor source writes, token changes, parallel pipeline or media resubmissions.
rollback: Revert scoped dispatcher commit; keep current native archives; stop concurrent production rather than routing through another identity.
notes: Source-use prompt propagation does not prove semantic compliance; final system qualification is unchanged. Independent acceptance remains separate from repair.
